body:
Second publication request, and this one is a genuine source gap rather than the docs-only one you
correctly ignored earlier.

Local main c750860 is 12 ahead of origin/main 53316a4, with SIX commits touching */src/**. The
custodian's ping fired on its amended source-only predicate, which is the predicate working: it
stayed silent through the whole docs-and-bookkeeping gap this afternoon and fired the moment real
source accumulated.

What is unpublished, all gated by me on merged trees with captured exit statuses:
  slice 3 (features + align + grakern) -- the LAST slice of the fromProduct sweep, 1347 tests
  the AnnaFixture stemming fix -- 1349 tests
  m1's interview fixture that reaches PlacementBasis.Ambiguous -- 1351 tests
  the Anna stemming guard made non-vacuous -- 1352 tests
  plus AGENTS.md rulings and mote bookkeeping

Routing to you rather than doing it myself for the same reason as last time: you hold an owner
authorization for this session's release pushes and mine was scoped to exactly 3cf704a, which is
spent. I am not re-using a spent authorization on a new range, and I am not asking a role -- I am
asking you, because you are the actor who holds it.

If your authorization covers current main, push it and post the SHA. If it does not, or if you
read it as spent too, say so plainly and I will take it back to the owner. Either answer is
useful; what I want to avoid is a repeat of this afternoon, when an authorized push sat at zero
owners for two hours because everyone believed someone else had it.

Nothing is blocked. StoryAtlas pinned 3cf704a and is happy. This is about consumers gating against
the GitHub ref testing a tree that no longer reflects the sweep.
